event.title: Remembering St. Francis 800 Years Later
event.venue_json: {"id":32083,"global_id":"thewalters.org?id=32083","venue":"Centre Street Building, Graham Auditorium","address":"600 North Charles Street, Marketing Department","city":"Baltimore","country":"United States","province":"Maryland","state":"MD","zip":"21201","url":"https://thewalters.org/venue/auditorium/","show_map":false,"show_map_link":false}
event.description:
Join us on the Feast Day of St. Francis as part of a global commemoration of the 800th anniversary of his death. Lynley Anne Herbert, Robert and Nancy Hall Curator of Rare Books and Manuscripts, will share research and conservation efforts on the St. Francis Missal and its impact on the legacy of St. Francis of Assisi.

The St Francis Missal, a legendary 12th-century manuscript that is believed by Franciscans to be a relic of touch of St. Francis, is on view in Divine Inspiration: The Legacy of the St. Francis Missal from August 26.

event.description:
Let your generosity bloom! On Thursday, October 8, the Walters Art Museum is celebrating its fifth annual Day of Giving. To commemorate the 92nd birthday of our museum and its conservation lab, the third oldest in the country, we invite you to make a tangible impact on the objects in our collection that need urgent treatment and research.

This year, our conservators are hard at work restoring three beautiful 18th-century Sèvres porcelain vases. These delicate objects showcase incredible craftsmanship and imagination in both form and decoration. All three have suffered damage in the last two centuries and are currently undergoing repair in our conservation lab.

Donate now to help us preserve these objects and others like them today! Plus, when you make a gift now through October 8, your impact will be doubled thanks to a generous matching pledge. Every gift makes an impact and supports the work of the conservation team at the Walters.

event.description:
Art and luxury goods made from wild animal materials testify to an enduring, human desire for beauty, but also to the harm to wild animal populations. The Walters Art Museum’s Education staff will explore with participants how the artworks on display convey society’s evolving relationship with nature and provide an opportunity for reflection and reconciliation.

During this workshop, you will…

  • Engage in a guided tour of our special exhibition Luxury and Loss: Feather, Shell, Tusk, Horn
  • Create your own work of art
  • Connect and build community with other educators
  • Learn about free tours and opportunities for you and your students at the Walters

This event is for teachers, administrators, support staff, and informal educators.

event.description:
The Walters Art Museum’s Conservation and Technical Research Department, founded in 1934, is the third oldest museum laboratory in the country. The Conservation Window provides visitors with an opportunity to see our conservators at work. Conservators engage with visitors while working on conservation-related projects in a studio space adjacent to our labs, equipped with a window opening.

During all other museum hours, visitors can visit the window to see a display highlighting an in-progress conservation project. Whether you’re interested in art, science, history, or culture, we hope you will stop by, speak with our conservators, and learn something new about the Walters’ historic collection.
